concept_card.statement: Waves from two slits add or cancel, giving fringes of width beta = lambda D / d; energy is only redistributed.
concept_card.analogy: Like rearranging chairs: some rows fill, others empty, none added.
steps: Bright at path difference n lambda, dark at (n + 1/2) lambda
Cover one slit and fringes vanish

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: If the slits are closer, the fringes should be closer and thinner too.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: It seems the pattern should shrink with the slits, like a smaller stamp making a smaller print.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: With closer slits the path difference grows more slowly along the screen, so you move farther to gain one wavelength. Hence beta = lambda D / d, which goes as 1/d.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: A smaller slit gap d gives wider fringes, since beta = lambda D / d.
remediation_cards.sim_moment: Double Slit: drag the d slider down and watch the fringes spread apart.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: Interference makes extra light at bright fringes and destroys light at dark ones.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: Bright fringes really are up to four times as bright as one slit alone, so light seems added.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: Energy is conserved. Each slit gives I0, so 2I0 on average. Interference only moves energy: bright fringes reach 4I0, dark ones 0, and the average stays 2I0.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: Interference redistributes light energy across the screen; it never creates or destroys it.
remediation_cards.sim_moment: Double Slit: toggle 'cover one slit' and compare where the light goes with one slit versus two.

remediation_cards.wrong_idea: Covering one slit just removes half the fringes.
remediation_cards.why_it_feels_right: It feels like each slit makes its own share of fringes.
remediation_cards.why_wrong: Every fringe needs waves from both slits meeting. With one slit nothing adds or cancels, so no fringes, only the broad single-slit diffraction pattern of the open slit.
remediation_cards.correct_idea: Fringes need both slits; cover one and the whole fringe pattern disappears.
remediation_cards.sim_moment: Double Slit: flip the 'cover one slit' toggle and watch all fringes merge into one broad band.

contrast_probes.probe: When the slits are moved closer, what is the main thing that changes on the screen?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: The fringes get narrower and more crowded.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: More light energy gets made, so the bright fringes get brighter.

contrast_probes.probe: Ravi's screen now shows fewer, more crowded-looking fringes; did he move the slits closer or cover one slit?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: He moved the slits closer, so the fringes squeezed together.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: He covered one slit, so half the fringes went away.

contrast_probes.probe: After one slit is covered, what do you expect at the spot where the brightest fringe used to be?
contrast_probes.reply_if_first: Hardly any light, because that light was being made by the two beams interfering.
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: Still a bright fringe, the pattern is just cut down to half.

contrast_probes.probe: If Ananya halves the gap between the slits, what happens to the fringe width?
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: It doubles, because beta = lambda D / d.

contrast_probes.probe: The bright fringes are four times as bright as one slit alone; where did that extra light come from?
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: It was taken from the dark fringes, so the total stays the same.

contrast_probes.probe: If one slit is taped over, will you still see alternating bright and dark fringes?
contrast_probes.reply_if_second: No, the fringes vanish and only a broad band of light from the open slit remains.
